HMW-V15: Vendor Quantity Reconciliation

How might we let vendor operators flag cargo quantity discrepancies — when their measured numbers differ from what Teleport has on record — without giving them write access to Teleport's records?
Context: When a vendor completes a job and Teleport's records show 24 bags / 1,280 kg but the vendor's driver measured 24 bags / 1,295 kg at pickup, there is a discrepancy. Right now this surfaces only at invoice time — too late, and only via WhatsApp or email. VUS-033 requires vendors to see Teleport's quantities for verification. The question is whether (and how) vendors should be able to flag a discrepancy while the job is Completed or Verified. The data model must keep Teleport's values authoritative — vendors cannot edit them — but the platform needs a structured mechanism to surface disagreements before billing disputes.

Option A: Parallel Vendor Measurement Inputs

Structured
Display Teleport's quantities as the authoritative record. Below each value, show a "Your count" input field the vendor fills in. Values that match are shown in green; mismatches trigger an inline red badge and enable a "Submit discrepancy" button with a mandatory note field. The discrepancy record is stored separately (not overwriting Teleport's data) and visible to admin in the admin slide-out.
Pros
• Most structured signal for admin: specific numbers, not just "something is wrong"
• Side-by-side comparison makes diff obvious at a glance
• Vendor enters their actual measurement — admin can accept or reject the correction
• Works well for finance reconciliation at end of month (structured data)
Cons
• More visual weight in the Cargo section
• Vendor must fill in all fields, even matching ones, to submit a single-field discrepancy
• Risk: vendor enters numbers to "flag" but their own count is also inaccurate

Option B: Per-Quantity Flag Buttons

Surgical
Keep the Cargo section compact. Add a small "Flag" button next to each individual quantity. Clicking a specific flag opens a micro-form inline: vendor's measured value + optional note. More targeted than Option A — the vendor only enters the field they dispute, not all three. Admin sees a specific "weight disputed: 1,280 kg → 1,295 kg" record.
Pros
• Lower friction: vendor only fills in the disputed field
• Admin immediately knows which field is wrong
• Cargo section stays compact when no dispute is active
• More surgical = less likely to create noise/false disputes
Cons
• Discoverability: small flag buttons may be missed
• Doesn't reveal the comparison until clicked (no overview of matches/mismatches)
• Harder to verify multiple disputes at once
• Interaction complexity: each field has its own expand/collapse state

Option C: General Dispute Note

Simplest
Show the Cargo section as-is (read-only), but add a single "Report discrepancy" button at the bottom of the section. Clicking it opens a freetext textarea. The vendor describes the issue in plain language ("We measured 1,295 kg not 1,280 kg"). Admin sees a note but must interpret it to know which field is wrong. Lowest friction; least structured.
Pros
• Minimal UI change — one extra button
• Flexible: vendor can describe any type of discrepancy (not limited to bags/weight/CBM)
• Matches the current informal WhatsApp workflow — just moves it in-app
• Easy to implement
Cons
• Unstructured: "weight was actually 1295" still requires admin to parse and identify the field
• Doesn't create diff-trackable records (harder to resolve and audit)
• No inline feedback about what matches vs what doesn't
• Not suitable for bulk reconciliation (e.g. "show me all jobs with disputed quantities")

Verdict: Option A — Parallel Vendor Measurement Inputs

Option A is the right pattern for a reconciliation-first platform. It produces structured, field-specific discrepancy records that admin can act on immediately — no interpretation required. Side-by-side display also makes it immediately obvious that bags match and weight doesn't, which reduces the round-trip of admin asking "which field is wrong?"

Option B is the right UX for a more mature product (v2+) where vendors understand the workflow — but in v1, the "parallel fields" approach reduces learning curve by mirroring how a vendor would compare numbers in Excel. Option C (freetext note) is adequate for v1 but doesn't scale to bulk reconciliation and can't power an admin-side "disputed quantities" filter.

Key implementation notes for Option A:
• Vendor measurement fields appear only in Completed or Verified status (reconciliation window).
• All three fields (bags/weight/CBM) are pre-filled blank. The mismatch badge only appears when the vendor's value differs from Teleport's.
• A discrepancy is submitted atomically — all three fields + optional note together — creating one discrepancy record per job, not one per field.
• The record stores: Teleport values, vendor values, note, timestamp, vendor company name. Admin sees it in the job slide-out under a "Quantity Discrepancies" row.
• Fields become read-only (with the mismatch state preserved) once discrepancy is submitted, until admin resolves it.

Open question: Should vendors be able to submit a discrepancy after Teleport has already verified the job? Verification locks the admin's records, but the vendor may discover the discrepancy late. Recommend: allow discrepancy submission at Verified state too — it creates a post-verification flag, not a re-opening of the record. Admin can then issue a correction or note in the activity log.
